G.S.R. 864(E).—In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1), 1(A) and (2) of Section 17 
of Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 (59 of 1960), the Committee for Control and Supervision 
of Experiments on Animals (hereinafter referred to as ‘Committee’), in supersession of the Experiments 
on Animals (Control and Supervision) Rules, 1968 vide Ministry of Food and Agriculture, Community 
Development and Co-operation (Department of Agriculture) notification no. 5-1/68/INS dated 14" 
September, 1968 and the Breeding of and Experiments on Animals (Control & Supervision) Rules, 1998 
vide Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment notification No. S.O. 1074 dated 15" December, 1998 
published in Extraordinary Gazette of India, hereby decided to amend the aforementioned rules, except as 
respect things done or omitted to be done before such supersession; 


Objections and suggestions, if any, may be communicated to the Member Secretary (CCSEA), 
Office of CCSEA, Near State Bank of India, Delhi Milk Scheme Complex, Shadipur, Delhi — 
110008 or by email cpcsea-mef@ gov.in within a period of thirty days. 


DRAFT RULES 
1. Short title and commencement. — (1) These rules may be called the Prevention of 
Cruelty to Animals (Control and Supervision of Experiment, Breeding and Trading of 
Laboratory Animals) Rules, 2026. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 
(3) These Rules will establish measures for the protection of animals used for scientific or 
educational purposes. 


(4) To that end, these rules lays down guidelines for the following: 


(a) the replacement and reduction of the use of animals in experiments and the refinement of 
the breeding, accommodation, care and use of animals in experiments; 

(b) the origin, breeding, marking, care and accommodation and euthanasia of animals; 

(c) the operation of breeders, traders and users; 


[भाग ॥--खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 45 


(9) the evaluation and authorisation of projects involving the use of animals in experiments 


(5) These Rules shall apply where animals are used or intended to be used in experiments or 
bred specifically so that their organs or tissues may be used for scientific purposes. 


(6) These Rules shall apply until the animals have been euthanized, rehabilitated to a suitable 
habitat or husbandry system upon completion of experimentation. 


(7) The elimination of pain, suffering, distress or lasting harm by the successful use of anaesthesia, 
analgesia or other methods shall not exclude the use of an animal in experiments from the scope 
of these Rules. 


(8) These Rules shall apply to live non-human vertebrate animals, including independent feeding 
larval forms of fishes, embryonated eggs and foetal forms of mammals as from the last third stage 
of their normal development; 


(9) These Rules shall apply to animals used in experiments, which are at an earlier stage of 
development than that referred to sub-rule 8, if the animal is to be allowed to live beyond that stage 
of development and, as a result of the experiments performed, is likely to experience pain, 
suffering, distress or lasting harm after it has reached that stage of development. 


(10) These Rules shall not apply to the following: 


(a) non-experimental agricultural practices; 

(b) non-experimental clinical veterinary practices; 

(c) veterinary clinical field trial required for the marketing authorization of a legally 
approved veterinary medicinal product except test batch and quality control trial for 
batch manufacturing; 

(d) practices undertaken for the purposes of recognised animal husbandry; 

(e) practices undertaken for the primary purpose of identification of an animal; 

(f) practices not likely to cause pain, suffering, distress or lasting harm equivalent to, or 
higher than, that caused by the introduction of a needle in accordance with good 
veterinary practice. 


2. Definitions. - In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires,- 
(a) “Act” means the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 (59 of 1960); 


(b) “Board” means the Animal Welfare Board of India established under section 4 and 
as reconstituted from time to time under section 5A of the Act; 


(c) “Breeder" means any natural or legal person registered with Committee breeding animals 
with a view to their use for in-house experiments or for the use of their tissue or organs for scientific 
purposes or supplying to other registered establishments whether for profit or not;

(d) “CCSEA” means the Committee for Control and Supervision of Experiments on Animals 
established under sub-section (1) of section 15 of the Act, (hereinafter referred to as “Committee); 


(e) “Chairman” means the Chairman nominated under sub-section (2) of section 15 of the Act; 


(f) "Collaborative Research" means any experiment undertaken between two or more research 
institutions solely for the purpose of advancement of scientific research for human or animal 
welfare; 


(g) "Contract Research" means any research undertaken by both domestic as well as foreign 
individual, company, firm, corporation or institution on behalf of an individual, company, firm, 
corporation or institution for consideration for profit or not; 


(h) “Experimentation” means any programme or project involving use of animal for acquisition 
of knowledge of a biological, physiological, ethological, physical or chemical nature; and includes 
the use of animal in the production of reagents and products such as antigens and antibodies, 
routine diagnostics, testing activity and establishment of transgenic stocks, for the purpose of 
saving or prolonging life or alleviating suffering or significant gains in wellbeing for people of the 
country or for combating any disease whether of human beings or animals; 


(i) "Establishment” means any installation, building, group of buildings or other premises, 
including a place that is not wholly enclosed or covered and mobile facilities, where laboratory 
animals are bred, housed, traded or used for experiments. 


(j) “Guidelines” means any documents or direction issued by the CCSEA from time to time to 
carry out the purpose of implementation of the Act or Rules made thereunder; 


(k) “Humane Endpoint” means a predetermined criterion that identifies when an animal's pain, 
suffering, distress, or impairment of well-being has reached a level at which action must be taken 
to prevent further suffering of animals and terminate the experiment. 


(1) "Institutional Animals Ethics Committee" means a body comprising a group of persons 
recognised and registered by the CCSEA in an establishment which is constituted and operated 
in accordance with experiments specified for the purpose by the Committee, (hereinafter referred 
to as “IAEC”’); 


(m) “Invasive experiment” means any procedure that involves animal restraint, blood collection, 
injection or any intervention that alters normal anatomy, or causes physiological interference by 
breaching the body’s natural barriers. Such procedures include, but are not limited to: Surgical 
interventions, such as organ transplantation, implantation of telemetry devices or catheters; Sample 
collection including blood or tissue sampling that requires significant incisions or deep punctures 
beyond routine veterinary practice; and Administration procedures such as repeated oral gavage 
or deep-tissue injections. 


(n) “Laboratory animals” means all vertebrate animals used or intended to be used in experiments

regulated under these Rules; 


(0) “Member” means a Member of the Committee for Control and Supervision of Experiments 
on Animals; 


(p) “Member-Secretary” means the Member-Secretary to the Committee for Control and 
Supervision of Experiments on Animals; 


(q) “Nominee” means the person selected by the Committee as its representative to carry out 
the work of CCSEA; 


(r) “Non-invasive experiment” mean experiments that do not involve any breach of the skin or 
surgical intervention and shall be employed wherever the scientific objective can be achieved 
without invasive procedures. Such experiments may include, inter alia, the use of non-invasive 
imaging techniques for monitoring physiological or pathological changes, the collection of 
biological samples such as faeces, urine or naturally shed hair for scientific analysis, and 
behavioural observation or monitoring of animals in non-restrictive environments without causing 
pain, distress or injury. 


(s) “Project” means a programme of work having a defined scientific objective and involving 
one or more experiments; 


(t) "Specified format" means the forms specified for the purpose by the Committee from time to 
time; 


(u) “Trader” means any natural or legal person registered with the Committee, supplying animals 
to the establishments registered with the Committee, with a view to their use in experiments or for 
the use of their tissue or organs for scientific purposes, whether for profit or not; 


(v) “User” means an establishment registered with Committee using animals in experiments, 
whether for profit or not; 


(w) “Veterinarian” means a person registered with Veterinary Council of India or State 
Veterinary Council, as the case may be, holding degree from a recognized Veterinary Institution. 
3. Replacement, Reduction and Refinement (3Rs). - For the purpose of implementation of 
principle of replacement, reduction and refinement (3Rs), the registered establishments carrying 
out the experiment shall ensure.- 


(1) that, wherever possible, a scientifically satisfactory method or testing strategy, not entailing 
the use of live animals, shall be used instead of an experiment; 


(2) that the number of animals used in projects is reduced to a minimum necessary to obtain 
scientifically valid and statistically reliable results without compromising the objectives of the 
project;

(3) that refinement of breeding, accommodation and care, and of methods used in experiments, 
eliminating or reducing to the minimum any possible pain, suffering, distress or lasting 
harm to the animals, adequate environmental enrichment, adoption of best veterinary 
practices and the use of validated humane endpoints. 


4. Purposes of Experiments.- Experiments may be carried out for the following purposes 
only: 

(1) basic research aimed at the advancement of knowledge, including fundamental research in 
biological, biomedical, behavioural or veterinary sciences. 


(2) translational or applied research with one or more of the following aims: 
(a) the avoidance, prevention, diagnosis or treatment of disease, ill-health or other 
pathological conditions or their effects on human beings, animals or plants; 


(b) the assessment, detection, regulation or modification of physiological conditions in 
human beings, animals or plants; or 


(c) the welfare of animals and the improvement of the production conditions for animals 
reared for agricultural purposes; 


(3) for any of the aims in sub-rule (2) in the development, manufacture or testing of the quality, 
effectiveness and safety of drugs, food and feed stuffs and other substances or products; 


(4) protection of the natural environment in the interests of the health or welfare of human 
beings or animals; 


(5) research aimed at preservation of the species; 


(6) higher education, or professional training for the acquisition, maintenance or improvement 
of vocational skills; 


(7) forensic investigations in accordance with the legal requirement. 


(8) Process of bleeding/blood products

not be used in experiments, with the exceptions of those experiments meeting the following

6. Experiment on non-human primates. - Subject to Rule 5, specimens of non-human primates 
shall not be used in experiments, except for those experiments meeting the following conditions.- 


(1) the experiment has one of the purposes referred to in- 


(a) clause (a) of sub-rule (2) or sub-rule (3) of Rule 4 of these Rules is undertaken with a 
view to the avoidance, prevention, diagnosis or treatment of debilitating or potentially 
life- threatening clinical conditions in human beings; or 


(b) sub-rule (1) or (5) of Rule 4; and 


(c) there is scientific justification to the effect that the purpose of the experiment cannot 
be achieved by the use of species other than non- human primates. 


Note: A debilitating clinical condition for the purposes of these Rules means a reduction in a 
person’s normal physical or psychological ability to function. 


(2) Specimens of non-human primates listed in the Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 
2022, shall not be used in experiments. 


7. Classification of severity of experiments. - 


(1) The establishment shall follow the severity of experiment, classified as ‘non-recovery’, 
‘mild’, ‘moderate’, or ‘severe’ on a case-by-case basis as set out in Annexure -I 


(2) The establishments shall ensure that an experiment is not performed if it involves severe 
pain, suffering or distress that is likely to be long period and cannot be ameliorated. 


8. Requirements for breeders, traders and users.- 


(1) No establishment shall carry out the business or house animals for breeding or trading of 
animals for the purpose of experiments unless it is registered with the CCSEA; 


(2) Every breeder, trader or establishment shall apply for registration through existing online 
portal developed by CCSEA for carrying out the business of: 


(i) breeding animals for the purpose of experiments 
(i1) trading of animals for the purpose of experiments, 
(iii) breeding and trading animals for the purpose of experiment 


(3) The Traders shall ensure that animals bred, procured and housed by the establishment are traded 
only to the CCSEA registered establishments on approval of the IAEC of the receiving 
establishment or Committee, as the case may be.

(4) The breeders and traders shall submit quarterly report to IAEC and annual report for each 
financial year in the prescribed form at schedule VII on or before 317 March of each year to the 
Committee. 


9, Registration of establishments conducting experiments on animals or housing, 
breeding and trading of animals for experimental purposes. — 


(1) No establishment shall perform any experiment on animals or house, breed and/or trade 
any animal for experiments unless it is registered with the CCSEA as per the provisions under 
these rule(s). 


(2) Every establishment performing experiments on animal(s) or housing, breeding and trading of 
animals for experimental purposes shall apply for registration, in prescribed format at schedule I 
through online portal of CCSEA to the Member Secretary with specified fees. 


10. Processing of applications.- (1) All the applications submitted as per Rule 9 in the office of 
CCSEA shall be processed as under: 


(a) The Member-Secretary shall verify the fact by himself or depute nominee of CCSEA or 
representative of CCSEA for verification of facts mentioned in the application for registration; 


(b) After receiving satisfactory report and information in Schedule IT, the Member Secretary shall 
register such establishment; 


(c) An establishment shall be duty-bound to comply with the conditions of registration, or any 
conditions prescribed by the Committee; 


(d) |The Committee shall take a decision on the registration within specified period as mentioned 
in the Administrative (Committee for Control and Supervision of Experiments on Animals) Rules, 
2023; 


(९) The Committee shall communicate the modification of facilities, if needed, before 
registration and taking the final decision on registration; 


(f) | Each establishment registered under Committee shall bear a unique registration code and 
number for each purpose; 


(g) The registration certificate issued to the establishment maintaining Animal House Facilities 
including the IAEC shall remain valid for three years unless its terminated or withdrawn by the 
establishment or Committee as the case may be. 


11. Permission of the Committee required for conducting experiments. — 

(1) Every establishment registered with CCSEA shall obtain permission either from the 
Committee or the Institutional Animals Ethics Committee before conducting experiment, as the 
case may be;

(3) | Every establishment conducting experiments which have been defined as mild and

(10) The animal(s) to be used for experimentation shall mandatorily be certified by the

of animals, severity of experiment or experimental procedure. 


12. Competency of personnel.- 


(1) Person in-charge or Head of the establishments shall ensure that each breeder, trader and 
user has sufficient staff on site. 


(2) The staff should be adequately educated and trained before they perform any of the following 
functions 


(a) carrying out experiments on animals; 
(b) designing experiments and projects; 
(c) taking care of animals; or 


(d) euthanasia of animals. 


Note: The establishment shall maintain proper documents in support of education, experience, 
registration of veterinarian and training. 


(3) Persons carrying out the functions referred to in clause (b) shall have received instruction in a 
scientific discipline relevant to the work being undertaken and shall have species-specific 
knowledge. 


(4) Staff carrying out functions referred to in clause (a), (c) or (d) shall be supervised in the 
performance of their tasks until they have demonstrated the requisite competence. 


(5) Establishment shall ensure, through authorisation or by other means, that the requirements 
laid down in this paragraph are fulfilled. 


(6) Establishment shall publish minimum requirements with regard to education and training and 
the requirements for obtaining, maintaining and demonstrating requisite competence for the 
functions set out in paragraph 2. 


13. Specific requirements for personnel.- 


(1) the Person in-charge or Head of the establishment shall ensure that each breeder, trader and 
user has one or several persons on site who shall: 


(a) be responsible for overseeing the welfare and care of the animals in the establishment; 


54

(b) ensure that the staff dealing with animals have access to information specific to the 
species housed in the establishment; 


(c) be responsible for ensuring that the staff are adequately educated, competent and 
continuously trained and that they are supervised until they have demonstrated the 
requisite competence. 


(2) Person in charge or Head of establishments shall ensure that personnel shall: 


(a) ensure that any unnecessary pain, suffering, distress or lasting harm that is being 
inflicted on an animal in the course of an experiment is stopped; and 


(b) ensure that the projects are carried out in accordance with the project authorisation or, 
in accordance with the application sent to the IAEC or CCSEA or any decision taken 
by the IAEC or CCSEA, and ensure that in the event of non-compliance, the 
appropriate measures to rectify it are taken and recorded. 


14. Designated veterinarian. - (1) The person in charge of establishments shall ensure that each 
breeder and user has appointed a veterinarian to advise and monitor the well-being and treatment 
of animals. 


(2) All experiments shall be performed under the supervision of a veterinarian. 


15. Procedures for experiments. - (1) The CCSEA shall issue detailed order or guidelines for 
experiments, or breeding or trading of an animal from time to time to minimize their pain and 
sufferings before, during and after the experimentation including rehabilitation and reuse; 


(2) The CCSEA shall also prescribe the specific standards for welfare of animals to be followed 
by the establishment for housing animals during and after the experiment on animals which shall 
be binding on the establishments; 


(3) The establishment shall not perform any experiment or use any chemical or agents which 
are banned by any authority and not required for testing. 


(4) As far as possible, death as the endpoint of an experiment shall be avoided and replaced by 
early and humane endpoints. If death as the endpoint is unavoidable, the experiment shall be 
designed so as to: 


(a) minimize the number of deaths of animals as much as possible; and 


(b) minimize as much as possible, the duration and intensity of suffering to the animal 
to ensure a painless death;

(c) every establishment must maintain a dedicated euthanasia registry detailing the date, 
species, exact method/chemical agent utilized, dosage, reason for termination, and the co- 
signatures of both the executing investigator and the Designated Veterinarian. 


16. Composition of Institutional Animals Ethics Committee (IAEC). — (1) Every establishment 
shall mandatorily constitute nine members for control and supervision of experiment, breeding, 
housing and trading which will be valid for three years. 


(2) The constitution of IAEC shall include a biologist, two scientists from different biological 
disciplines, a veterinarian involved in the care of animals, and the scientist in charge of animal 
facility from the respective establishments. The CCSEA shall nominate a main nominee, link 
nominee, scientist from outside the institute and socially aware nominee in the IAEC; 


(3) The nominees of CCSEA shall be selected from the list of nominees selected by CCSEA after 
due process; 


(4) The establishment shall nominate Chairperson and Member Secretary from amongst the 
internal members of [AEC except the nominated members by the CCSEA; 


(5) In addition to the above IAEC members, a specialist, in the relevant field, shall be co- 
opted while reviewing special projects using hazardous agents such as radio-active substances and 
deadly micro-organisms. Though, the co-opted member shall not be part of the decision making 
of the IAEC, their advice to be taken seriously before making any decision by IAEC. 


(6) IAEC shall not be required for Traders involved in supply of animals from breeders to the users 
without housing of animals. 


17. Conduct of business of IAEC.- (1) The Chairperson of IAEC shall convene minimum of two 
meetings of IAEC in a calendar year, requiring at least one meeting to be held in each half of a 


calendar year; 


(2) The quorum of the IAEC meeting shall be of six members wherein mandatory presence of 
Main Nominee and Socially Aware Nominee is must; 


(3) Link Nominee can attend any IAEC meeting in case Main Nominee conveys his/ her 
unavailability in writing to the Chairperson of IAEC. 


(4) Any decision taken in the meetings of IAEC without quorum shall be considered invalid; 


(5) The Chairperson is responsible for submission of minutes of the meeting of IAEC through 
the web portal within fifteen days from the date of the IAEC meeting as per Schedule V. 


18. Record keeping of experiments conducted. - 


(1) Every establishment shall maintain the records of animals utilized for Experiments in the

Schedule IV, animals bred or acquired for experimentation in the Schedule 11 and record of animal 
sold or transferred in the Schedule VII. 


(2) All such records shall be made available for inspection to the Committee or any other officer 
authorized by the Committee from time to time. 


19. Stocking of animals for experiments, breeding, housing and trading. - (1) The Committee 
shall prescribe technical parameters for stocking of animals including technical specifications for 
their housing but not limited to the following broad guidelines.- 


(a) Animal houses shall be located in a quiet atmosphere undisturbed by traffic, and the premises 
kept tidy, hygienic and the animals protected from drought and extremes of weather. 


(b) Animal cages for small animals and stables for large animals shall be made in such a manner 
that provides comfort to animals and not overcrowded. 


(c) Where standards have been laid down by the Committee, the cages, the stable, as the case 
may be, shall conform to those standards. 


(d) Detailed specifications for housing, feeding and maintenance of various species to be used 
in animal experimentation as notified by the Committee, shall be adhered by the registered 
establishment. 


(e) Each establishment shall provide species specific environmental enrichment and ethological 
needs. 


(f) Establishment housing large animals must maintain species-specific exercise and 
rehabilitation area as the case may be. 


(2) Registered establishments housing animals exposed to Risk Group HI or IV agents must 
maintain certified directional airflow and negative pressure integrity, subject to mandatory digital 
logging and annual verification by a specialized biosecurity engineer. 


20. Reporting by establishment.- The breeder-trader shall submit information pertaining to 
trading of animals in the prescribed format as mentioned in the Schedule VII annually before 31“ 
March of every year; or any other information sought by the Committee from time to time. 


21. Transfer and acquisition of animals for experiment. — (1) Any registered breeder, user 
or establishment under these rules shall transfer or sale or acquire any animal from the CCSEA 
registered breeder, establishment or trader only; 


(2) In the event of non-availability of a particular kind of livestock and farm animals (above level 
of Lagomorpha), fishes and birds, from the registered breeders or traders, they may be procured 
from non-registered establishments or open market with prior approval of [AEC and maintenance 
of documents provided such animals undergo a mandatory veterinarian-certified quarantine and 


[भाग ॥--खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 57 


stabilization period as prescribed by CCSEA guidelines prior to experimentation. 


(3) Animals that are not available in the country shall be permitted for sourcing from outside the 
country as per the provisions of the extant Import-Export policies/guidelines. 


22. Contract research on animals. — Any research institutions or agency not defined under the 
rules may also outsource research activities involving animals to an establishment duly registered 
under CCSEA. 


23. Renewal. - (1) Every establishment registered with CCSEA is required to be renewed after 
every three years along with the reconstruction of IAEC. 


(2) While considering the renewal, the CCSEA shall consider the minutes of IAEC meetings 
submitted by the establishment regularly for last three years along with the Annual Inspection 
Reports of the Animal House Facility by the nominee in the Schedule VIII vis-a-vis Annual 
statement of large animals use (as the case may be) submitted in Schedule IX for last three years. 


24. Periodical inspection of the establishment.- (1) It is binding on the main nominee and 
socially aware nominee to carry out periodical inspections not less than two times in a years, apart 
from the meeting, to oversee the animal house with regard to their fulfilment of the CCSEA 
guidelines, welfare of animals housed in the establishment; 


(2) The main nominee shall submit such inspection report as per Schedule VIII format annexed to 
these Rules; 


(3) Any violations of the CCSEA rules, guidelines and prescribed standards observed by the main 
nominee and socially aware nominee shall be reflected in the Minutes of the IAEC meeting and 
also reported to the CCSEA; 


(4) CCSEA shall also depute the inspection team to verify the compliance by the establishment, 
with prior intimation and such report shall be submitted as per Schedule IT format. 


25. Power to suspend or revoke registration. — (1) based on the periodical inspection report 
received from the main nominee or socially aware nominee in accordance with Rule 24 or any 
complaints made by any person, organization which have been verified through inspections, if 
there is a reason to believe that the provisions of the act or rules have been contravened, the 
committee shall.- 


(a) issue a deficiency notice specifying the nature of non-compliance and requiring corrective 
action within 15 days of issuance of notice; 


(b) where the establishment fails to comply with the deficiency noticed within 15 days or where 
repeated instances of violation occurred within six months, the Committee may, and after 
giving the establishment a reasonable opportunity of being heard, suspend or revoke the 
registration.

(b) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-rule (1) where the committee is satisfied that the 
non-compliance is limited to a specific project or protocol or unit or facility, it may restrict 
suspension or revocation to such project or protocol or unit or facility of the said establishment 
and permit the continued operation of unaffected and compliant activities subject to such 
conditions and enhance monitoring as it may deem fit. 


(c) Nothing in Rule 25 shall prevent the Committee from ordering immediate suspension or 
revocation, in whole or in part, where it is satisfied that there exists an imminent risk to the life, 
health, or welfare of the animals. 


26. Appeal. - (1) Establishment aggrieved with any decision of the committee may, if so desire, file 
an appeal to the Secretary of the Administrative Ministry of CCSEA, within thirty days of receipt 
of the decision; 


(2) The Secretary of the Administrative Ministry on receipt of the grievance, if so desire, shall 
after giving notice to the aggrieved establishment, hear the grievance, either by himself or herself 
or through a Committee and decide on the appeal to reject or allow citing the reasons in writing; 


(3) The decision of the Secretary of Administrative Ministry shall be treated as final decision 
regarding the grievance.

Classification of Severity of Experiments 


The severity of an experiment shall be determined by the degree of pain, suffering, distress or 
lasting harm expected to be experienced by an individual animal during the course of experiment. 


Section I: Severity categories.- 

1. Non-recovery: 
Experiments which are performed entirely under general anaesthesia from which the animal 
shall not recover consciousness shall be classified as ‘non-recovery’. 


2. Mild: 
Experiments on animals that are likely to experience short-term mild pain, suffering or 
distress, as well as experiments with no significant impairment of the well-being or general 
condition of the animals shall be classified as ‘mild’. 


3. Moderate: 
Experiments on animals as a result of which the animals are likely to experience short-term 
moderate pain, suffering or distress, or long-lasting mild pain, suffering or distress as well 
as experiments that are likely to cause moderate impairment of the well-being or general 
condition of the animals shall be classified as ‘moderate’. 


4. Severe: 
Experiments on animals as a result of which the animals are likely to experience severe pain, 
suffering or distress, or long-lasting moderate pain, suffering or distress as well as 
experiments, that are likely to cause severe impairment of the well-being, or general condition 
of the animals shall be classified as ‘severe’. 


Section II: Assignment criteria.- 

The assignment of the severity category shall consider any intervention or manipulation of an 
animal within a defined experiment. It shall be based on the most severe effects likely to be 
experienced by an individual animal after applying all appropriate refinement techniques. 


When assigning an experiment to a particular category, the type of experiment and several other 
factors should be considered. All these factors should be considered on a case-by-case basis. 


The factors related to the experiment shall include: 

(i) type of manipulation, handling, 

(ii) nature of pain, suffering, distress or lasting harm caused by (all elements of) the experiment, 
and its intensity, the duration, frequency and multiplicity of techniques employed, 


(iii) Cumulative suffering within an experiment,

MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
[N.F. Railway (Construction Organisation)] 
NOTIFICATION 
Maligaon, the 6th October, 2026 
S.O. 5463(E).— Whereas, by the Notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of 
Railways [N.F. Railway (Construction) Organization], vide No. 8.0. 2689 (E) dated 29" May, 2026 and corrigendum 
S.O. 3689 (E) dated 077 July, 2026 published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part-II, Section-3, Sub-Section 
(ii) issued under sub-section (l) of section 20A of the Railways (Amendment) Act, 2008 (no. |l of 2008) (hereinafter 
referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intention to acquire the land specified in the Schedule 
Annexed to the said Notification, is required for the purpose of execution, maintenance, management and operation of 
the Special Railway Project, namely, 'Aluabari Road - New Jalpaiguri 3" & 47 B.G. Line" in the district of 
Kishanganj, in the State of Bihar; 

And whereas, the substance of the said Notification has been published in the daily newspapers, namely, 
Prabhat Khabar on 26/07/2026 under sub-section(4) of Section- 20A of the said Act; 

And whereas, no objection has been received from any person by the Competent Authority; 

And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (l) of Section-20E of the said Act, the Competent Authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 

Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the Competent Authority and in exercise of the power 
conferred by sub-section (l) of Section-20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the Schedule annexed to this Notification should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 

And, further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of Section-20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on Publication of this Notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the Schedule annexed to 
this Notification shall vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

the objector an opportunity of being heard, either in person or by a legal practitioner and may, after hearing such 
objections and after making such further enquiry, if any, asthe Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either 
allow or disallow the objections.

final.

अहमदाबाद में पश्चिम रेलवे के भावनगर डिवीजन के साबरमती डी केबिन - सर्खेज सेक्शन (21 किमी) दोहरीकरण कार्य” 
नाम की विशेष रेल परियोजना के निष्पादन के लिये आवश्यक है, ऐसी भूमि के अर्जन करने के आशय की घोषणा करती है; 


उक्त भूमि के कोई हितबद्ध व्यक्ति, राजपत्र में इस अधिसूचना के प्रकाशन की तारीख से तीस दिन के भीतर, उक्त 
अधिनियम की धारा 20D की उप-धारा (|) के अधीन उपर्युक्त प्रयोजन के लिए ऐसी भूमि के अर्जनज और उपयोग के संबंध में 
अपनी आपति प्रकटकर सकेगा; 


ऐसी प्रत्येक आपति सक्षम प्राधिकारी एवं अतिरिक्त विशेष द्वितीय भूमि अधिग्रहण अधिकारी, प्रथमतल, आपदा 


प्रबंधन भवन, महसूल भवन, कलेक्टर ऑफिस, सुभाषत्रिज सर्कल के पास, अहमदाबाद को लिखित रुप मे किया जाएगा जो

MINISTRY OF RAILWAY 
[Western Railways (Construction Organization)] 
NOTIFICATION 
Mumbai, the 7th October, 2026 
G.S.R. 866(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (I) of section 20A of the 
Railways Act, 1989 (24 of 1989) (hereinafter referred to as the said act), the Central Government after being satisfied 
that for the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which has been given in the schedule annexed hereto, is 
required for execution of the Special Railway Project, namely “Doubling of Sabarmati D Cabin - Sarkhej Section 
(21 KM) on Bhavnagar Division of Western Railway in District of Ahmedabad, State of Gujarat”, hereby 
declares its intention to acquired such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within a period of thirty days from the date of publication of this 
Notification in the Official Gazette, raise objection to the acquisition and use of such land for the aforesaid purpose 
under sub-section (I) of section 20D of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, Second Additional Special Land 
Acquisition Officer, First Floor, Disaster Management Building, Collector Office, Near. Subhash Bridge Circle, 
Ahmedabad in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof and the Competent Authority shall give the objector an 
opportunity of being heard, either in person or by legal practitioner and may after hearing all such objections and after 
making such further enquiry, if any as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the 
objections.

NOTIFICATION 
Mumbai, the 7th October, 2026 


G.S.R. 867(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section(I) of section 20A of the Railways 
Act, 1989 (24 of 1989) (hereinafter referred in as the said act 2008), the Central Government after being satisfied that 
for the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which has given in the schedule annexed hereto, is required for 
execution of the Special Railway Project, namely,3rd and 4th line between vadodara-ratlam (258.94 km) in District 
Vadodara in the State of Gujarat, hereby declares its intention to acquired such land; 


Any Person Interested In The Said Land May, Within A Period Of Thirty Days From The Date Of Publication 
Of This Notification In The Official Gazette, Raise Objection To The Acquisition And Use Of Such Land For The 
Aforesaid Purpose Under Sub-Section(I) Of Section 20d Of The Said Act; 

Every such objection shall be made to the competent authority, namely, “Special Land Acquisition Officer, jila 
Sevasadan office Panchamahal, District Panchmahal’, in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof and the competent 
authority shall give the objector an opportunity of being heard, either in person or by legal practitioner and may after 
hearing all such objections and after making such further enquiry, if any as the competent authority thinks necessary, 
by order, either allow or disallow the objections; 


Any order made by the competent authority under sub-section (II) of section 20(D) of the said act shall be final. 


The land plans and other details of the land covered under this notification are available and can be inspected 
by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the competent authority.

NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 30th September, 2026 
G.S.R. 868(E).— The following draft of the Motor Vehicles (Registration and Functions of Vehicle Scrapping 
Facility) Rules, 202l, which the Central Government proposes to make in exercise of the powers conferred by section 
59(4) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 988 (59 of 988), is hereby published as required by sub-section (l) of section 22 
of the said Act for information of all persons likely to be affected thereby; and notice is hereby given that the said draft 


rules shall be taken into consideration after the expiry of thirty days from the date on which the copies of this notification 
as published in the Official Gazette, are made available to the public; 


Objections and suggestions to these draft rules, if any, may be sent to the Additional Secretary (Transport), 
email: comments-morth @ gov.in, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Transport Bhawan, Parliament Street, New 
Delhi-!0 OOL. 


The objections or suggestions which may be received from any person in respect of the said draft rules before 
the expiry of the aforesaid period will be considered by the Central Government. 


DRAFT RULES 


I. Short title and commencement. - (|) These rules may be called the Motor Vehicles (Registration and Functions of 
Vehicle Scrapping Facility) Amendment Rules, 2026. 


(2) These rules shall come into force on the date of publication of the notification in the Official Gazette. 


2. In rule l0, in sub-rule (), for clause (xiii), the words "Government-owned vehicle or" shall be omitted.

MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
(Central Railway) 
NOTIFICATION 
Mumbai, the 6th October, 2026 
Under clause 20A of the Railways Act, 1989 (24 of 1989) 


5.0. 5490(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of Section 20A of the Railways Act, 
1989 (24 of 1989) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for the 
public purpose, the land, the brief description of which has been given in schedule annexed hereto, is required for 
purpose of execution, maintenance, management and operation of Special Railway Project, namely “3" and 4" line 
between Pune-Solapur-Wadi (394.91Km)” in the Kalaburagi district of Karnataka State, hereby declares its 
intention to acquire such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within a period of thirty days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, raise objection to the acquisition and use of such land for the aforesaid purpose 
under sub-section (1) of section 20D of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority namely, Assistant Commissioner, 
Kalaburagi, District Kalaburagi, Karnataka in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof, and the Competent 
Authority shall give the objector the opportunity of being heard, either in person or by legal practitioner and may, after 
hearing such objections and after making such further enquiry, if any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by 
order, either allow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 20D of the said Act shall be 
final. 


The land plans and other details of the land covered under this notification are available and can be inspected 
by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

धारा 30 की उपधारा (2) के खंड (ड) द्वारा प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, भारत अंतर्राष्ट्रीय माध्यम केंद्र (रजिस्ट्रार, 


काउंसिल और अन्य अधिकारियों और कर्मचारियों के पदों की संख्या और भर्ती) नियम, 2022 का और संशोधन करने के 
लिए निम्नलिखित नियम बनाती है, अर्थात्‌ :-- 


1. (1) इन विनियमों का संक्षिप्त नाम भारत अंतर्राष्ट्रीय माध्यस्थम्‌ केंद्र (रजिस्ट्रार, काउंसिल और अन्य अधिकारियों और 
कर्मचारियों के पदों की संख्या और भर्ती) संशोधन नियम, 2026 है। 
(2) ये राजपत्र में उनके प्रकाशन की तारीख को प्रवृत्त होंगे । 


2. भारत अंतर्राष्ट्रीय माध्यम केंद्र (रजिस्ट्रार, काउंसिल और अन्य अधिकारियों और कर्मचारियों के पदों की संखया और 
भर्ती) नियम, 2022 (जिन्हें इसमें इसके पश्चात्‌ उक्त नियम कहा गया है), नियम 12 को उसके उपनियम (1) के रूप में 
पुन:संख्यांकित किया जाएगा और,--

(क) इस प्रकार पुन:संख्यांकित उपनियम (1) में, “सेवा की अन्य शर्तों के मामलों में केंद्र के अधिकारियों और 
कर्मचारियों की सेवा की शर्तें, ऐसे नियमों और विनियमों के अनुसार विनियमित की जाएंगी,” शब्दों के स्थान पर, 
“सेवा की अन्य शर्तों, जिनके लिए इन नियमों में कोई अभिव्यक्त उपबंध नहीं किया गया है, के मामलों में केंद्र के 
अधिकारियों और कर्मचारियों की सेवा की शर्तें, ऐसे नियमों और विनियमों के अनुसार विनियमित की जाएंगी,” 
शब्द रखे जाएंगे; 


(ख) इस प्रकार पुन:संख्यांकित उपनियम (1) के पश्चात्‌ निम्नलिखित उपनियम अंतःस्थापित किया जाएगा, 
अर्थात्‌ :--

G.S.R. 869(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (e) of sub-section (2) of section 30 of the 
India International Arbitration Centre Act, 2019 (17 of 2019), the Central Government hereby makes the following 
rules to amend the India International Arbitration Centre (Number of Posts and Recruitment of Registrar, Counsels 
and other Officers and Employees) Rules, 2022, namely: - 


1. (1) These rules may be called the India International Arbitration Centre (Number of Posts and Recruitment of 
Registrar, Counsels and other Officers and Employees) Amendment Rules, 2026. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. In the India International Arbitration Centre (Number of Posts and Recruitment of Registrar, Counsels and other 
Officers and Employees) Rules, 2022 (hereinafter referred to as the said rules), rule 12 shall be renumbered as sub- 
rule (1) thereof and, - 


(a) in sub-rule (1) as so renumbered, for the words “other conditions of service, shall be regulated”, the words 
“other conditions of service for which no express provision has been made in these rules, shall be regulated”, 
shall be substituted; 


(b) after sub-rule (1) as so renumbered, the following sub-rule shall be inserted, namely: - 


“(2) Any officer or employee, may by giving notice of forty-five days in writing, resign from his office, or 
the Centre may, by giving notice of forty-five days, for reasons to be recorded in writing, direct any officer 
or employee to relinquish his office.”.

NOTIFICATION 
Mumbai, the 6th October, 2026 
Under clause 20A of the Railways Act, 1989 (24 of 1989) 


S.O. 5489(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of Section 20A of the Railways Act, 
1989 (24 of 1989) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for the 
public purpose, the land, the brief description of which has been given in schedule annexed hereto, is required for 
purpose of execution, maintenance, management and operation of Special Railway Project, ४३37 and 4" line between 
Pune-Solapur-Wadi (394.91Km)” district of Karnataka State, hereby declares its intention to acquire such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within a period of thirty days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, raise objection to the acquisition and use of such land for the aforesaid purpose 
under sub-section (1) of section 20D of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority namely, Assistant Commissioner, Sedam, 
District Kalaburagi, Karnataka in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof, and the Competent Authority shall 
give the objector the opportunity of being heard, either in person or by legal practitioner and may, after hearing such 
objections and after making such further enquiry, if any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either 
allow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 20D of the said Act shall be 
final. 


The land plans and other details of the land covered under this notification are available and can be inspected 
by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

करने की रीति) नियम, 2026 के अधीन, यथास्थिति, उस तारीख से, जिस दिन उक्त आदेश पारित किया गया था / या अपील 
में उसकी पुष्टि/उपांतरित किया गया था, साठ दिनों के भीतर जमा नहीं की गई है; 


अतः आपको इस सूचना की प्राप्ति की तारीख से दिनों के भीतर नीचे विनिर्दिष्ट रीति में 
रुपये की उक्त रकम का संदाय करने या उसे जमा कराने की अपेक्षा की जाती है। 


जमा करने की रीति और स्थान: 


यह ध्यान दें कि ऊपर विनिर्दिष्ट अवधि के भीतर उक्त रकम जमा न करने की स्थिति में, उक्त नियमों के नियम 14 के 
उप-नियम (2) के अधीन उस जिले के कलेक्टर को वसूली प्रमाणपत्र अग्रेषित किया जाएगा, जिस क्षेत्र में आप निवास करते 
हैं, या कारबार करते हैं, या अभिलाभ के लिए काम करता हो, या जहां संपत्ति का मालिक है, और यह रकम वसूली की लागत 
सहित, आपसे भू-राजस्व के बकाया के रूप में वसूल की जाएगी।

MINISTRY OF TEXTILES 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 8th October, 2026 


G.S.R. 873(E).— Whereas the draft Textiles Committee (Adjudication of Penalties and Appeal) Rules, 2026 
were published, as required under sub-section (1) of section 22 of the Textiles Committee Act, 1963 (41 of 1963), vide 
notification of the Government of India, in the Ministry of Textiles, number G.S.R.746(E), dated the 18th August, 2026, 
published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part I, Section 3, Sub-section (i), dated the 19th August, 2026, inviting 
suggestions or objections from all persons likely to be affected thereby, before the expiry of a period of thirty days from 
the date on which the copies of the Official Gazette containing the said notification were made available to the public; 


And whereas, copies of the said Official Gazette were made available to the public on the 19th August, 2026; 


And whereas, the said period of thirty days has expired and no objections or suggestions were received from 
the public on the said draft rules for consideration by the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by clauses (ea) and (eb) of sub-section (2) of section 22 read with 
sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 17A of the Textiles Committee Act, 1963 (41 of 1963), the Central Government 
hereby makes the following rules, namely:— 


1. Short title and commencement.— (1) These rules may be called the Textiles Committee (Adjudication and Manner 
of Holding Inquiry and Imposition of Penalty) Rules, 2026. 


(2) The rules shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 
2. Definitions.— (1) In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires,— 


(a) “Act” means the Textiles Committee Act, 1963 (41 of 1963); 
(b) “adjudicating officer” means the officer appointed as such under section 17A of the Act; 
(c) “appellate authority” means the officer appointed as such under sub-section (2) of section 17A of the Act; 


(d) “Collector” means the Collector of a district and includes any officer appointed or authorised by the State 
Government to discharge the functions of the Collector; 


(e) “Form” means a form appended to these rules. 


(f) “notice of demand” means a notice issued by the adjudicating officer in the prescribed Form-V requiring a person 
liable to pay any monetary penalty under the Act to pay the amount specified therein within the period specified 
in such notice; 


(2) The words and expressions used in these rules and not defined but defined in the Act, shall have the same meanings 
respectively assigned to them in the Act; 


3. Complaint.— (1) The Secretary, Textiles Committee or an officer of the Textiles Committee duly authorised by him 
in writing, on the basis of any report, inspection or reference received, may file a complaint in such format as specified 
in Form-I through electronic means or speed post with registration and proof of delivery or by hand to the adjudicating 
officer regarding any contravention committed under section 17 and section 18 of the Act. 


(2) Upon receipt of the complaint the adjudicating officer shall record the details of such complaint in the complaint 
register. 


4. Holding inquiry and imposing penalty.— (1) For the purpose of adjudication under sub-clauses (i) and (1) of clause 
(b) of sub-section (2) of section 17 of the Act and ascertaining whether any person has committed any contravention as 
specified in that section, the adjudicating officer shall issue a notice in Form-II to such person requiring him to show 
cause within such period as may be specified in such notice, being not less than seven days from the date of service 
thereof, as to why an inquiry should not be held against him. 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 13 


(2) Every notice under sub-rule (1) shall indicate the nature of contravention alleged to have been committed. 


(3) The concerned person may submit his reply together with the supporting documents within a period of 
fifteen days from the date of receipt of the notice. 


(4) After considering the cause, if any, shown by such person, if the adjudicating officer is of the opinion that 
an inquiry should be held, he shall issue a notice requiring the appearance of that person personally or through a 
representative duly authorised by him on such date as may be fixed in the notice. 


(5) On the date fixed, the adjudicating officer shall explain to the person proceeded against or his authorised 
representative, the contravention committed by such person and the provision of the Act in respect of which 
contravention is alleged to have been committed. 


(6) The adjudicating officer shall, then, give an opportunity to such person to produce such documents or 
evidence as specified in Form-III as he may consider relevant to the inquiry and if necessary, the hearing may be 
adjourned to a future date and in taking such evidence the adjudicating officer shall not be bound to observe the 
provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (47 of 2023). 


(7) While holding an inquiry under these rules, the adjudicating officer may require and enforce the attendance 
of any person acquainted with the facts and circumstances of the case to give evidence or to produce any document 
which in the opinion of the adjudicating officer may be useful for or relevant to the subject matter of the inquiry. 


(8) If any person fails, neglects or refuses to appear before the adjudicating officer as required under sub-rule 
(4), the adjudicating officer may proceed with the inquiry in the absence of such person after recording the reasons 
thereof. 


5. Order of adjudicating officer.— (1) If, upon consideration of the evidence produced before the adjudicating officer, 
the adjudicating officer is satisfied that the person has committed the contravention, he may, by order in writing, impose 
such penalty under the Act as he considers reasonable. 


(2) Every order made under sub-rule (1) shall specify the provision of the Act in respect of which 
contravention has been committed and shall contain the reasons for imposing the penalty. 


(3) A copy of the order made under this rule and all other copies of proceedings shall be supplied free of 
cost to the complainant and the person against whom the inquiry was held. 


(4) The adjudicating officer shall complete the proceedings within six months from the date of issuance of 
the notice to the opposite party. 


6. Factors to be considered while imposing penalty.— While determining the quantum of penalty under sub-section 
(2) of section 17 of the Act, the adjudicating officer may have due regard to the following factors, namely: — 


(a) the nature and gravity of the contravention; 

(b) whether the contravention is a first-time, repeated or continuing contravention; 
(c) the extent of loss or damage, if any, caused by the contravention; 

(d) any mitigating circumstances placed on record; and 


(e) any other factors as may be considered appropriate by the adjudicating officer. 


7. Copy of Order.— The adjudicating officer shall send a copy of every order made under these rules by him to the 
person on whom the penalty is imposed and to the Chairman of the Committee, Joint Secretary to the Government of 
India (ex-officio member of the Committee) and Secretary, Textiles Committee. 


8. Service of notices and orders.— (1) A notice or an order issued under these rules shall be served on the person 
against whom an inquiry is held, in any of the following manner, namely:— 


(i) by delivering or tendering it to such person or his authorised representative; or 


(ii) by sending it to such person through electronic means or by speed post with registration and proof of 
delivery to the address of his place of residence or his last known place of residence or the place where he 
carried on or last carried on business or personally works or last worked for gain; or 


(iii) if, it cannot be served in the manner specified under clause (i) or clause (ii), by affixing it on the outer door 
or some other conspicuous part of the premises in which that person resides or is known to have last resided or

witnessed by two persons. 


9. Appeal.— (1) Any person aggrieved by an order of the adjudicating officer under these rules, may prefer an appeal 
to the appellate authority under sub-section (2) of section 17A of the Act in such format as specified in Form-IV.

The appeal shall be filed with the appellate authority within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt 
of such order: 


Provided that, the appeal may be admitted after the expiry of the period of thirty days, if the appellant 
satisfies the appellate authority that he had sufficient cause for not preferring the appeal within such 
period. 


The appeal shall be accompanied by a copy of order of the adjudicating officer issued under sub-rule (1) 
of rule 5 and a clear statement of facts appealed against, the grounds for appeal and the relevant section 
of the Act. 


The appeal shall be filed in triplicate by the appellant in person or by his duly authorised representative 
in writing duly appointed in this behalf or by speed post with registration and proof of delivery or through 
electronic means. 


The appeal sent by post shall be deemed to have been filed to the appellate authority on the day it is 
received. 


If on scrutiny, the appeal is found to be in order, it shall be admitted and if the appeal is found to be 
defective, the same shall, after notice to the party, be returned for compliance and if within a period of 
twenty-one days of receipt of such notice or within such extended time as may be granted, the defect is 
not rectified, the appellate authority, may, for reasons to be recorded in writing, decline to admit the 
appeal. 


A copy of the appeal shall be served by the appellate authority on the respondent, by hand or by speed 
post with registration and proof of delivery or through electronic means. 


The respondent may, within a period of thirty days of service of notice of appeal, file reply to the appellate 
authority. 


The appellate authority may call for the records relating to the proceedings from the respective 
adjudicating officer. 

The appellate authority may, after giving the parties to the appeal an opportunity of being heard, pass 
such orders as he may consider reasonable. 


The appellate authority shall dispose of the appeal within a period of sixty days from the date of filing of 
such appeal. 


10. Order of appellate authority.— (1) After considering the submissions of the parties, the evidence, and the records 
of the case, the appellate authority shall pass an order for reasons to be recorded in writing.

(5) The decision of the appellate authority shall be final and binding. 


11. Extension of time.— The adjudicating officer or the appellate authority may, for reasons to be recorded in writing, 
where there is a reasonable cause for the delay or failure to act, extend any period specified in these rules till such period 
as he considers reasonable. 


12. Order.— Every order under these rules, shall be dated, signed and communicated to all the parties. 


13. Rectification of the order.— The adjudicating officer or the appellate authority who has passed an order, may 
rectify any error apparent on the face of the record in such order, either on its own motion or where such error is brought 
to his notice by the affected person within a period of fifteen days from the date of such order. 


Explanation: For the purpose of this rule, “error apparent on the face of record” shall mean any typographical 
errors that creep in inadvertently into the order and includes such other errors that do not require a long drawn out 
reasoning process to ascertain such a mistake. 


14. Manner of recovery of penalty.— (1) Where a penalty is imposed by the adjudicating officer under the Act, and 
in the event of filing of an appeal such an order is confirmed by the appellate authority, and such penalty is not deposited 
within the period of sixty days from the date of passing the order, or the order was confirmed in appeal, as the case may 
be, the adjudicating officer shall issue a notice of demand in such format as specified in Form-V to the person liable to 
pay the penalty. 


(2) If the amount is not paid within the period specified in the notice of demand under sub-rule (1), the adjudicating 
officer shall forward a recovery certificate to the Collector of the district in which the defaulter resides, or carries on 
business, or works for gain, or owns property. 


(3) On receipt of the certificate under sub-rule (2), the Collector shall proceed to recover the amount stated in 
it, together with the cost of recovery, as an arrear of land revenue, in accordance with the Revenue Recovery Act, 1890 
(1 of 1890), or other applicable laws for the time being in force.

NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 8th October, 2026 
8.0. 5510(E).— In exercise of powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highways 
Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for 
the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the Schedule below, is required for building 
(widening/two lane with paved shoulder/four laning etc.,), maintenance, managementand operation of Newly Proposed 


in the stretch of land from Km. 6.836 to Km. 64.77 (Collectorate Campus on SH14 Bharatpur Road Deeg Rajasthan 
321203) in the district of Deeg in the state of RAJASTHAN, hereby declares its intention to acquire such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within twenty-one days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, object to the use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub -section(1) of 
section 3C of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, Additional District Collector Deeg in 
writing and shallset out the grounds thereof and the Competent Authority shall give the objectoran opportunity of being 
heard, either in person or by a legal practitioner, and may, afterhearingallsuch objections and after making such further 
enquiry, if any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 3C ofthe said Act shall be final. 


The land plans and other details of the land to be acquired under their notification are available and can be 
inspected by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 8th October, 2026 

5.0. 5519(E).— In exercise of powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highways 
Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for 
the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the Schedule below, is required for building 
(widening/two lane with paved shoulder/four laning etc.,), maintenance, management and operation of NH-166 in the 
stretch of land from Km. 67.140 to Km. 145.300 (Ratnagiri-Kolhapur Section) in the district of KOLHAPUR in the 
state of MAHARASHTRA, hereby declares its intention to acquire such land. 

Any person interested in the said land may, within twenty-one days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, object to the use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub-section(1) of 
section 3C of the said Act. 

Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, Sub Divisional Officer, Panhala in 
writing and shall set out the grounds thereof and the Competent Authority shall give the objector an opportunity of 
being heard, either in person or by a legal practitioner, and may, after hearing all such objections and after making 
such further enquiry, if any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the 
objections. 

Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 3C of the said Act shall 
be final. 

The land plans and other details of the land to be acquired under their notification are available and can be 


inspected by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

9.0, 5526(E).— Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport 
and Highways, 3528(E) Dated:01/07/2026 , published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, 
Sub-section (ii) issued under sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) 
(hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intension to acquire the land specified in 
the Schedule annexed to the said notification for building (widening/four-laning, etc.), maintenance, management and 
operation of NH354 in the stretch of land from Km. 0 to Km. 44.154 in the district of AMRITSAR in the state of 
PUNJAB 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in “The Tribune (English)” dated 
09/07/2026 , “Jagbani (Punjabi)” dated 09/07/2026 ; under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said Act; 


And whereas the Competent Authority has received objections filed under Section 3-C, considered and 
settled the same appropriately; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule shall 
vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

management and operation of National Highway No. 716 on the stretch of land from Km. 52.730 to Km. 101.620 
(Kadapa to Renigunta Section) in the district of Tirupati in the State of Andhra Pradesh.

And whereas no objection has been received from any person by the Competent Authority; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the Competent Authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the Competent Authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule shall

New Delhi, the 8th October, 2026 


5.0. 5535(E).— Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport 
and Highways, 4829 Dated:22/0/2025 , published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub-section 
(ii) issued under sub-section (l) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 956 (48 of 956) (hereinafter referred to 
as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intension to acquire the land specified in the Schedule annexed to 
the said notification for building (widening/four-laning, etc.), maintenance, management and operation of NH 748A in 
the stretch of land from Km. 89.900 to Km. 36.00 in the district of BAGALKOT in the state of KARNATAKA 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in “The Times of India” dated 
30/0/2025 , “VijayKarnataka” dated 30/0/2025 ; under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said Act; 


And whereas the Competent Authority has received objections filed under Section 3-C, considered and settled 
the same appropriately; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (l) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (l) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule shall vest 
absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

CHAPTER II 


PROCEDURE FOR SANCTION OF BUILDING PLANS AND RELATED 
DOCUMENTATION 


BUILDING SANCTION REQUIRED. — (1) No person shall carry out any erection, re- 
erection, additions or alterations to any building or cause the same to be done without 
obtaining a sanction for such work from the Competent Authority. 


Any sanction issued by the Competent Authority shall be valid for the period as 
provided under Section 243 of the Act. 


In case of land being held on lease from the Central Government or the Board, no building 
sanction shall be given if the proposed building contravenes lease conditions. 


PROCEDURE FOR OBTAINING BUILDING SANCTION. — (1) An applicant who 
intends to erect or re-erect a building or to make additions or alteration in any building shall 
give notice in writing to the Executive Officer, by registering himself/herself in the e- 
Chhawani portal and apply through online, duly enclosing all requisite documents and plans,

refusal of building application will be made within 30 days in case of buildings located

appertaining to such site; or

scheme sanctioned under Section 240 of the Act;

constitutes a breach of terms of the entrustment of management or contravenes any of 
the instructions issued by the Government regarding the management of the land by 
the Board; or

lease from the Government, if the right to build on such land is in dispute between the 
person applying for sanction and the Govt.;

plan shall be sanctioned, nor shall any development permit be issued, for any plot with 
an area less than the prescribed minimum;

existing plots less than 50 square meter which shall be eligible for building plan

CHAPTER V 
INCLUSIVE DESIGN 


FACILITIES IN THE PUBLIC BUILDING FOR THE DIFFERENTLY ABLED 
PERSON.— 

These Bye-Laws are applicable to all buildings, recreation areas and facilities used by public. 
It does not apply to private domestic residences. 


Site planning.— Level of the roads, access paths and parking areas shall be described in 
the plan along with specification of materials. Every building should have at least one access 
to main entrance/exit to the differently abled person which shall be indicated by proper 
signage. This entrance shall be approached through a ramp together with stepped entry. The 
ramp should have a landing after every 9 meter run and in front of the doorway. Minimum 
size of landing shall be 1.0 x 2.0 meter. 


Access path/walk way.— Access path from plot entry and surface parking to building 
entrance shall be a minimum of 1.8 meter wide having even surface without any step. Slope, 
if any shall not have gradient greater than 5%. Selection of floor material shall be made 
suitably to attract or to guide visually impaired persons (limited to floor material whose color 
texture is conspicuously different from that of the surrounding floor material or the material 
that emit different sound to guide visually impaired persons. Finishes shall have a non-slip 
surface with texture traversable by a wheel chair. Curbs wherever provided should blend to 
common level. 


Parking.— For parking of vehicles of differently abled persons, the following provisions 
shall be made: 


(a) Surface parking for two Equivalent Car Spaces (ECS) shall be provided near entrance 
for the differently abled person with maximum travel distance of 30 meter from building 
entrance; 


(b) The width of parking bay shall be minimum 3.6 meter; 


(c) The information stating that the space is reserved for wheel chair users shall be 
conspicuously displayed; 


(d) Guiding floor materials shall be provided or a device which guides visually impaired 
persons with audible signals or other devices which serves the same purpose shall be 
provided.

Building Requirements.— The specified facilities for the buildings for differently abled

(a) Approach to plinth level; 

(b) Corridor connecting the entrance exits for the differently abled person; 
(c) Stair-ways; 

(d) Lift;

(f) Drinking water; 

(g) Braille signage shall be provided at the above specified facilities. 


Approaches to Plinth Level.— (a) Ramp shall be provided with non-slip material to enter 
the building minimum clear width of ramp shall be 1.8 meter with maximum gradient 1: 12, 
between top and bottom of the ramp. Length of ramp shall not exceed 9.00 meters having 
0.8 meter high handrail on both sides extending 300 millimeter beyond the ramp. Minimum 
gap from the adjacent wall to the handrail shall be 50 millimeter; 


(b) Minimum clear opening for the entrance door shall be 1.0 meter. Threshold shall not be 
raised more than 12 millimeter; 


(c) For stepped approach, size of tread shall not be less than 300 millimeter and maximum 
riser shall be 150 millimeter. Provision of 0.8 meter high handrails on both sides of the 
stepped approach similar to the ramped approach shall be made. 


Corridor connecting the entrance/exit for the differently abled person.— The corridor 
connecting the entrance/exit for differently abled person leading directly outdoors to a place 
where information concerning the overall use of the specified building can be provided to 
visually impaired person either by a person or by signs, shall be provided as follows: 


(a) Guiding floor materials shall be provided or devices that emit sound to guide visually 
impaired persons; 


(b) The minimum width shall be 1.5 meter; 

(c) Incase there is a difference of level, slope ways shall be provided with a slope of 1:12; 
(d) Handrails shall be provided for ramps/slope ways. 

Stairways.— Stairways with open riser and provision of nosing shall not be sanctioned. 


Lifts.— Whenever lift is required as per Bye-Laws, provisions of at least one lift shall be 
made for the wheel chair user with the following car dimensions of lift recommended for 
passenger lift for 13 person’s capacity by Bureau of Indian Standard: 


(a) Clear internal depth minimum of 1.1 meter;

differently abled person with essential provision of washbasin near the entrance for the 
differently abled person. The minimum size shall be 1.5 meter x 1.75 meter: 


(a) Minimum clear opening of the door shall be 0.9 meter and the door shall swing or sliding 
type; 


(b) Suitable arrangement for vertical/horizontal handrails with 50 millimeter clearance from 
wall shall be made in the toilet; 


(c) The water closet seat shall be 0.5 meter from the floor. 


(10) Refuge.— An alternative to immediate evacuation of a building via staircases and/or lifts is 
the movement of differently abled persons to areas of safety within a building. If possible, 
they could remain there until the fire is controlled and extinguished or until rescued by fire 
fighters: 


(a) A refuge area may be provided at the fire protected stair landing on each floor that can 
safety hold one or two wheelchairs; 


(b) The area shall have doorways with clear opening width of 900 m; and 


(c) The area shall have an alarm switch installed between 900 millimeter and 1200 
millimeter from the floor level.

ENERGY CONSERVATION MEASURES.— (1) Use of Compact Florescent Lamps and 
Electric Chokes: 


(a) The use of incandescent lamps and conventional chokes in all new buildings, institutions 
constructed in Government sector, Government Aided sector, Boards and Corporations 
and Autonomous bodies is banned with immediate effect; 


(b) It will be mandatory that in these existing buildings the defective incandescent lamps and 
chokes when replaced would be replaced by only compact fluorescent lamps (CFL) and 
electronic chokes; 


(c) The Competent Authority will effect necessary modification in the local demand notices 
within two months time from the issue of this notification to promote the use of Compact 
Fluorescent Lamps and electronic chokes instead of conventional bulbs and chokes while 
releasing/sanctioning new connections/loads in such buildings. 


All new cases shall be sanctioned only if they have the following provisions for solar water 
heating systems: 


(a) An open space in the roof which receives direct sunshine; the roof shall have a load 
bearing capacity of at least 50 kg. per square meter; 


(b) The building must have a provision for continuous water supply to the solar water heating 
system; 


(c) The building design should provide for an insulated pipeline from the heating system to 
all distribution points where hot water is required; 


(d) The recommended minimum capacity of installation shall not be less than 25 litres per 
day for each bathroom and kitchen subject to the maximum of 50% of the total roof area 
is utilized by the system; 


(e) Installation of Solar Assisted Water Heating Systems shall confirm to BIS specification 
IS 12933. The solar collectors used in the system shall have the BIS certification mark. 


Whenever hot water requirement is continuous auxiliary arrangement either with electrical 
elements or oil based systems of adequate capacity may be provided. 


No new building in the following categories in which there is a system of hot water supply 
shall be sanctioned unless this installation has a solar assisted water heating system: 


(a) Industries which use hot water for processing; 
(b) All hospitals and nursing homes; 


(c) All hostels, hotels, motels, guest houses and banquet halls;

में, उस बिंदु तक जहाँ बाहरी दीवार की बाहरी सतह, ढलान वाली छत की तैयार सतह को काटती है; और सड़क की 
ओर मुख वाले गेबल के मामले में, छज्जे के स्‍तर और शिखर के बीच का मध्य बिंदु। वास्तुशिल्प विशेषताएँ, चिमनियाँ, 
पानी की टंकियाँ और अन्य सजावटी विशेषताएँ, जो मानव निवास के लिए अभिप्रेतनहीं हैं और सजावट के अलावा 
कोई अन्य कार्य नहीं करती हैं, ऊँचाई मापने के प्रयोजन से बाहर रखी जाएँगी; और यदि भवन किसी सड़क से सटा 
हुआ नहीं है, तो ऊँचाई भवन के चारों ओर और उससे सटे ज़मीन के औसत स्तर के ऊपर मापी जाएगी; 


"भवन रेखा" से वह रेखा अभिप्रेत है, जहाँ तक किसी सड़क, सड़क के विस्तार, या भविष्य की सड़क से सटे भवन का 
प्लिंथ (नींव का चबूतरा) विधिपूर्ण रूप से बढ़ाया जा सकता है; और इसमें किसी भी योजना में विहित (यदि कोई हो) 
रेखा भी सम्मिलित है; 


"भवन आवरण" से वे क्षैतिज सीमा अभिप्रेत हैं, जहां तक किसी भूखंड पर भवन के निर्माण की अनुमति दी जा सकती 
है: जो इन उप- विधियों में विहित स्पष्ट सेटबैक (पीछे हटने की दूरी) से अधिक नहीं होंगी; 


निर्मित क्षेत्र" का अर्थ है भवन द्वारा सभी मंजिलों पर घेरा गया कुल क्षेत्रफल; इसमें Hfectraz (cantilevered) भाग 
और मेज़ानाइन (mezzanine) मंजिलें (यदि कोई हों) शामिल हैं, लेकिन वे क्षेत्र शामिल नहीं हैं जिन्हें इन विनियमों

लीजहोल्ड या पढ़े पर दिए गए बंगले स्थित हैं; 


"व्यावसायिक भवन" का अर्थ है कोई भी भवन या भवन का कोई ऐसा हिस्सा, जिसका उपयोग व्यावसायिक लेन-देन 
करने, खातों और अभिलेखों को रखने, या इसी तरह के अन्य उद्देश्यों के लिए किया जाता है; दफ़्तर, बैंक, पेशेवर 
संस्थान, अदालतें, रिकॉर्ड और संदर्भ पुस्तकालयों को इस समूह में वर्गीकृत किया जाएगा, जहाँ तक इनका मुख्य काम 
सार्वजनिक कामकाज का लेन-देन करना और किताबें व रिकॉर्ड रखना है; 

“बुचरी” का मतलब एक बूचड़खाना है, जहाँ जानवरों (भेड़ और बकरियों) को किसी सक्षम अधिकारी की देखरेख में 
काटा जाता है; 

"केबिन" से अभिप्रेत है बिना रहने के उद्देश्य से बना ऐसा घेरा जो भार न सहने वाले और बिना चिनाई वाले पार्टीशन

“कार्पेट एरिया” (Carpet area) का मतलब किसी अपार्टमेंट का इस्तेमाल करने लायक कुल फ़र्श का एरिया है। इसमें 
बाहरी दीवारों का एरिया, सर्विस शाफ़्ट के नीचे का एरिया, खास बालकनी या बरामदे का एरिया और खास खुली

“कैनोपी” (Canopy) से एक ऊपरी छत या कोई ऐसी संरचनाजिसके ऊपर कपड़े या धातु की कोई कवरिंग लगी हो, 
जो धूप, ओले, बर्फ और बारिश जैसी मौसम की स्थितियों से छाया या आश्रय प्रदान करने में सक्षम हो। कैनोपी एक

“छत की ऊँचाई” (Ceiling Height) से तैयार फर्श और छत के बीच की ऊर्ध्वाधर (सीधी) दूरी अभिप्रेत है;
